newsitem.title: HONG KONG: China Res hit high on stronger outlook.
newsitem.headline: China Res hit high on stronger outlook.

text.p: Shares of China Resources Enterprise Ltd hit an all-time high on hopes for stronger earnings after it agreed to buy a 10 percent stake in container terminal operator HIT Investment Ltd from parent, brokers said.
"Anticipation of stronger future earnings growth due to an enlarged income base and an increase in its asset value after the purchase, boosted buying," said a sales manager at a regional brokerage.
China Resources shares, which resumed trade on Wednesday after a half-day suspension, were up HK$1.20 or 9.27 percent at HK$14.15 in mid-morning after hitting a high of HK$14.50.
Volume was 7.17 million shares worth HK$96.23 million.

"Anticipation that the company will grow stronger and bigger, and a growing importance of this kind of Chinese enterprises especially those relating to port business after the 1997 handover, underpinned strong buying interest," said Sean li, associate director from Amsteel Securities.

China Resources Enterprise said it has agreed to buy a 10 percent stake of HIT Investments from its parent China Resources (Holdings) Co Ltd (CRH) for HK$3.5 billion. It said it would fund the purchase by HK$2.25 billion in cash and the issuance of 111.11 million new shares at HK$11.25 per share to CRH.
CRH also agreed to place 90.90 million existing shares it held in China Resources Enterprise at HK$11.25 a share to private investors.
